page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core using x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of RAM, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance primarily in the average tier for multi-core operations, while showing strong single-core CPU performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2931.08, whereas the multi-core score of 11737.55 falls in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds at 553.22 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 49.73 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 36.88 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-8 offers a dense compute profile with dedicated CPU allocation, making it suitable for workloads that require consistent CPU performance without the overhead of excess memory. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its average score of 8037.0 in Clang compilation and 569.63 tokens/second in small-model LLM prompt processing.
